whyVerde.title: We're not just another firm. We're your team.
whyVerde.body1: Rafael Verde founded this firm to be the firm his own family wished they'd had — one that picks up the phone, explains what's happening in plain language, and treats each case like it's personal. Because it is.
whyVerde.body2: We don't subcontract our intake. We don't use call centers. When you call, you reach someone who speaks your language and knows your case.

bilingual.title: 100% Bilingual Team
bilingual.desc: We communicate in your language. Spanish is our first language, not a translation.

national.title: Nationwide Coverage
national.desc: We represent clients in all 50 states from our Miami headquarters — in person, remote, or hybrid.

free.title: Free Consultation
free.desc: We evaluate your case at no cost. No pressure. No obligation. Ever.

tech.title: Modern Technology
tech.desc: Real-time case tracking on Verde+ — our platform built for immigrants.

process.title: Four steps. No retainer until we agree on a plan.

step1.title: Free Consultation
step1.desc: Tell our team what's happening. Day or night, English or Spanish. A real person picks up.

step2.title: Case Evaluation
step2.desc: One of our attorneys reviews your situation and lays out your options — honestly.

step3.title: Legal Preparation
step3.desc: We build your strategy, draft filings, and prepare every piece of evidence your case needs.

step4.title: Full Representation
step4.desc: We argue, we file, we appear — all the way to the end. You focus on your family.

attorneyFeature.name: Rafael Verde
attorneyFeature.body1: Rafael Verde founded Verde Law straight out of Georgetown Law with one belief: that quality legal representation is a right, not a luxury. Immigrants who are afraid, who can't pay $15,000 upfront, who don't speak English — they deserve the same attorney who'd fight for a corporate client.
attorneyFeature.body2: Seven years and 600+ families later, the mission hasn't changed. Rafael still personally reviews every new case. He still answers messages on weekends. He built the firm he wished his own grandmother had when she arrived in this country with nothing.
